walkthrough:
Integrate the derivative with respect to $x$:
$$y = \int kx^{-1/2} dx = \frac{kx^{1/2}}{1/2} + c = 2k\sqrt{x} + c$$

Substitute the known points $P(1, -1)$ and $Q(4, 4)$ into the curve equation:
$$\text{At } P(1, -1): \quad -1 = 2k\sqrt{1} + c \implies 2k + c = -1$$
$$\text{At } Q(4, 4): \quad 4 = 2k\sqrt{4} + c \implies 4k + c = 4$$

Subtract the first equation from the second to solve for $k$ and $c$:
$$2k = 5 \implies k = 2.5 = \frac{5}{2}$$
$$c = -1 - 2(2.5) = -6$$

State the complete equation of the curve:
$$y = 5\sqrt{x} - 6$$
